transcript: Meeting header: 2026-10-07 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m
Participants: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sofia (CSM); Alex, Priya, Jordan, Samir (BlueWave)
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining the capacity pulse. We'll do a quick readout on last week's pilot runs, then walk sizing and autoscale policy updates.
[00:13] Alex: Hey Maya, thanks. We ran the 8k token summary workload overnight — saw a couple of spikes but generally ok.
[00:22] Priya: Quick note — timing is tight on our end, Jordan needs assurance on cost before exec sync next Friday.
[00:34] Jordan: Yep, cost and an SLO for tail latency please. If we blow budget during telehealth peak it's a blocker.
[01:05] Liam: Totally. Today we'll show an updated Dedicated sizing table and two autoscale strategies: conservative (maintain latency SLO) and cost-first (allow transient tail).
[01:30] Samir: Also want to confirm KV cache behavior during bursts — we saw cache thundering in one run, not sure if it's a runtime bug or our pattern.
[01:48] Maya: Good callout. We'll cover cache warming and prefix caching recommendations. Liam, can you share the spreadsheet link?
[02:12] Liam: Yep, shared: drive.google.com/bluewave-redwood/pilot-autoscale-v2 (note: internal link). Spreadsheet has per-model qps/sec, 95th latency, token costs and bridge rows for burst sizing.
[02:45] Alex: I see the conservative and burst columns. How are you modeling burst capacity — instantaneous GPU spin-up or pre-warmed pool?

[03:02] Liam: We model two mechanisms: pre-warmed pool (reserved, warm 1-3 instances depending on model size) and fast-burst via short-lived provisioning (30–90s ramp). For Dedicated the pre-warmed pool is recommended if burst probability > ~5%.
[03:34] Priya: What's the cost delta for pre-warmed? Our initial calc says about +18% on monthly runrate.

[03:50] Maya: That's in the sheet — we show incremental cost percentage per pre-warmed GPU. But note, pre-warmed reduces tail latency and prevents cold-KV penalties which can cause downstream retries and larger cost.
[04:12] Jordan: Can you explain the cold-KV penalty? We saw a few 5xxs during a spike correlated with higher token counts.

[04:28] Liam: Sure — when a model's KV cache isn't populated, the runtime needs to recompute attention and can't use prefix cache, so initial requests in a series are heavier. We suggest client-side sticky sessions and server-side prefix caching for predictable patterns.
[04:55] Samir: On sticky sessions — we use an ALB + session affinitiy; will that map to Redwood Dedicated nodes or do we need to do something special?
[05:10] Liam: With Dedicated you can set routing policy to prefer same pool by session key; we recommend hashing on conversation id. That plus a small pre-warmed set reduces cross-pool cache misses.
[05:30] Alex: Nice. On autoscaling policies I see options: threshold-based CPU/GPU, token-rate based and forecast-based. Which do you suggest for telehealth with daily peaks?

[05:45] Maya: For telehealth, forecast-based + scheduled scale is best. You should schedule pre-warm 10 minutes before expected clinic start; forecast handles anomalies. Conservative threshold policies tend to react too late for 30–90s cold starts.
[06:05] Priya: Our ops team wants to avoid scheduled scale-ups if it increases cost too much. Is there a hybrid?

[06:18] Liam: Yes — hybrid: keep a minimal pre-warmed baseline and allow forecast-driven burst to add capacity during expected peaks. We also support a short burst window where we accept slightly higher cost but maintain SLA.
[06:33] Jordan: Can you quantify what 'slightly higher cost' means?

[06:40] Liam: In your pilot usage profile, the spreadsheet shows that a 20% pre-warmed pool reduces 95th latency from ~420ms to ~170ms and increases cost by ~12% for the period. If you rely solely on fast-burst, cost might be lower on average but tail latency spikes to >800ms for first few requests.
[07:06] Alex: The numbers make sense. One anomaly — on 9/30 run we saw a spike where latency stayed elevated even after scale. Any idea why?

[07:20] Liam: That looks like cold-cache propagation across replicas plus an upstream retry loop. We noted repeated retries from your client before backoff triggered — those retries kept thrashing the pool. We recommend exponential backoff client-side and rate-limiting at edge.
[07:42] Samir: We do have a retry middleware that's pretty aggressive. We'll adjust backoff. Good catch.

[07:55] Maya: Switching topics — quantization and model variants. For cost reduction we proposed a 4-bit quantized variant for background summarization traffic and full-precision for synchronous telehealth summaries.
[08:12] Priya: How reliable is the quality delta? We can't have hallucination regressions for clinical notes.

[08:24] Liam: We ran evals — the quality drop for short summarization (<512 tokens) was minimal on our test prompts. For clinical-critical flows we recommend using full fp16 or a validated 4-bit variant after A/B test. Redwood Optimize can help run continuous evals and alert on regressions.
[08:48] Jordan: Can you show where in the sheet the recommended default pool sizes are?

[08:56] Liam: Yes, row labels: model-name | qps | baseline-instances | prewarm-count | burst-max-instances. For 'medical-summary-v1' we recommend baseline 4 gpus, prewarm 1 gpu, burst up to 10 GPUs for a 5min window.
[09:18] Alex: Baseline 4 GPU feels high vs our dev runs. Are you assuming production concurrency?

[09:26] Liam: Production concurrency assumes average of 80 concurrent users, each request ~1.2 qps ~ 0.2 tokens/s on average because of streaming; we modeled for 95th token throughput. We can parameterize lower if your concurrency is less.
[09:45] Maya: Quick poll — is the team comfortable with a 2-step approach: 1) apply conservative baseline with small pre-warm, 2) run a scheduled peak test next week and iterate?
[09:58] Priya: Yes, that sounds sensible.
[10:06] Samir: We want to simulate sudden 6x traffic bursts to validate fallback. Does Redwood support automatic fallback to a smaller, cheaper model if the main model is saturated?

[10:20] Liam: Yes — routing policies allow model fallback. You can set an automatic fallback to an embedding or distilled model with a config that preserves minimal functionality. We also support gradual degradation: reduce max tokens, switch to faster variant, then to cached responses.
[10:43] Alex: Can we get a runbook for fallbacks? Our on-call needs specifics: thresholds, who to notify, and what client behavior to expect.
[10:55] Maya: We'll include a draft runbook in the follow-up — I'll add it to the sheet as a separate tab.
[11:06] Jordan: One more security/enterprise item — audit logs and retention. For Dedicated we need 12 months of per-request logs (pseudonymized). Can you confirm retention options?

[11:20] Maya: Dedicated supports configurable retention up to multi-year; logs can be shipped to your S3 or SIEM. For pseudonymization we support token-level redaction or field-level redaction before export.
[11:35] Priya: KMS integration?
[11:38] Liam: Yes, we can integrate with AWS KMS or customer HSM for key wrapping. We'll send the security pack (SOC2 + KMS notes) after the call.
[11:52] Alex: Great. Now a couple of nitty gritty items observed in the metrics: request-queue length spikes at ~18:xx each day. That's your forecast horizon right?
[12:06] Liam: That aligns with the clinic shift change. We recommend a scheduled incremental pre-warm 12 minutes before shift start to smooth the queue curve.

[12:20] Maya: Let's talk about SLOs — BlueWave wants 95th latency < 250ms and 99th < 800ms. Given current runs, conservative policy hits 95th ~170ms as Liam said. 99th is closer to 720ms with pre-warm. Does that meet your internal bar?
[12:42] Jordan: 99th at 720ms is borderline. We want to push that down if possible. What's needed to get it under 600ms?

[12:52] Liam: Two levers: increase pre-warmed pool by one instance and enforce stronger sticky routing; also reduce cross-model co-location to avoid noisy neighbors — those steps should get 99th under 600ms for the tested workload.
[13:11] Priya: Cost for that extra instance?
[13:14] Liam: Incremental monthly cost ~3.5% of the Dedicated baseline in the sheet for that model family.
[13:23] Alex: Ok. On telemetry — can we get per-route token cost breakdown in console?
[13:30] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost by route and model; we can give you a short demo or export of last week's breakdown.
[13:44] Samir: For the upcoming test we want more telemetry: per-request trace with KV-hit/miss flag. Can Redwood emit that?
[13:54] Liam: We can emit traces with custom annotations: kv_hit=true/false, model_variant, queue_time_ms. We'll attach a sample trace format in the follow-up.
[14:10] Alex: There's one oddity: embedding requests seem to spike during async batches and impacted the serving pool. How to isolate embedding workers?

[14:22] Liam: We recommend isolating embeddings into a separate Dedicated pool or use Redwood batching/caching layer. If embeddings are high-volume asynchronous jobs, moving them to a dedicated queue avoids interference.
[14:37] Priya: We'll likely separate those. Good.
[14:44] Maya: Quick housekeeping — action items recap will be posted in the CRM. Sofia, can you add the meeting notes?
[14:51] Sofia: On it, I'll paste the key rows and next steps.
[15:00] Jordan: About the pilot timeline — assuming we run the scheduled peak test on 10/14 and results look good, what are lead times for Dedicated capacity changes?

[15:13] Maya: For Dedicated we can provision additional capacity within 48–72 hours for typical regions, or faster for committed bursts. If you require hard SLAs for lead time we'll scope reserved add-ons.
[15:30] Alex: One more question: does Redwood support regional fallback? If us-east is overloaded, can traffic route to us-west?
[15:40] Liam: Yes. Smart routing policies can route by latency, cost and region preference. For sensitive data you can restrict to the same region if required by residency.
[15:56] Priya: Data egress cost when cross-region?
[16:00] Liam: There's an egress delta in the cost model; we included a cross-region surcharge example in the sheet.
[16:12] Alex: Okay. Any open questions from the BlueWave team?
[16:18] Samir: We'll need the prefilling script for prefix caching. Do you provide client libs?
[16:26] Liam: We have a small sample script in the SDK for cache prefilling and session sticky hashing. I'll put it in the repo and share the link.
[16:40] Jordan: About fallbacks again — can we run an experiment where 10% of traffic goes to a distilled model to measure quality impact?
[16:50] Maya: Absolutely, Redwood supports canary traffic splits. We can schedule a controlled canary during a low-risk window and collect metrics.
[17:05] Alex: Great. Let's schedule that after the 10/14 test.
[17:15] Priya: One operational concern — who on Redwood will own the pilot SLA once we commit to Dedicated?
[17:23] Maya: CSM Sofia will be primary for day-to-day and Liam as the escalation SE, with me as AE for commercial touches.
[17:34] Sofia: I'll set up weekly syncs post-test and a Slack channel for on-call.

[17:44] Maya: Okay, quick recap and next steps — I'll read them out. 1) Maya to update cost model and send by 10/12. 2) Liam share perf traces and SDK cache scripts by 10/10. 3) BlueWave to run scheduled peak test on 10/14 and share logs by 10/15. 4) Sofia to post runbook and meeting notes. 5) Schedule canary of distilled model after test.
[18:20] Jordan: That works. Please call out anything that requires exec sign-off in the email.
[18:27] Maya: Will do. Any final questions?
[18:32] Alex: None here. Thanks everyone.
[18:35] Priya: Thanks, bye.
[18:37] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the sheet and artifacts. End call.
